# 1-Week Deload Protocol

## Overview
Your client transitions from a high-volume hypertrophy block into a strategic deload week. This maintains movement patterns and neural efficiency while allowing systemic recovery—critical before the next intensification phase. Volume drops to ~40% of previous load; intensity (RPE) drops to 6–6.5. Exercise selection remains identical to preserve motor learning and readiness.

---

## Deload Week Structure

**Training Frequency:** 4 sessions (same split as hypertrophy block)  
**Session Duration:** 35–45 minutes  
**RPE Target:** 6–6.5 across all work sets  
**Volume Reduction:** 6–8 working sets per session (~55% reduction)

---

## Session-by-Session Breakdown

### **Session 1: Lower Body (Quad-Dominant)**

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load | RPE | Notes |
|----------|-------------|------|-----|-------|
| Back Squat | 3 × 5 | 60% of hypertrophy working weight | 6 | Smooth, controlled tempo; 3-second descent |
| Leg Press | 2 × 8 | 65% | 6 | Reduce range slightly if needed for comfort |
| Leg Extension | 2 × 10 | 60% | 6 | Slow eccentrics; no lockout strain |
| Calf Raise (standing) | 2 × 12 | 70% | 6 | Maintenance only |

**Accessory/Mobility:** 5 min foam rolling (quads, IT band), 3 min couch stretch each side

---

### **Session 2: Upper Body (Horizontal Push/Pull)**

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load | RPE | Notes |
|----------|-------------|------|-----|-------|
| Bench Press | 3 × 5 | 60% of hypertrophy working weight | 6 | Pause 1 second at chest; no explosive drive |
| Barbell Rows | 3 × 5 | 60% | 6 | Controlled eccentric; chest to bar |
| Dumbbell Flyes | 2 × 8 | 50% | 6 | Reduce range of motion slightly |
| Face Pulls | 2 × 12 | 65% | 6 | High reps for shoulder health |

**Accessory/Mobility:** 5 min band pull-aparts, 3 min thoracic rotation stretches

---

### **Session 3: Lower Body (Deadlift/Hamstring-Dominant)**

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load | RPE | Notes |
|----------|-------------|------|-----|-------|
| Conventional Deadlift | 2 × 3 | 60% of hypertrophy working weight | 6 | Touch-and-go; no explosive intent |
| Romanian Deadlift | 2 × 6 | 60% | 6 | Emphasize stretch; minimal knee bend |
| Leg Curl (machine) | 2 × 10 | 60% | 6 | Controlled throughout |
| Sled Push | 2 × 12 | 65% | 6 | Light, steady pace |

**Accessory/Mobility:** 5 min glute activation (band walks, clamshells), 3 min hamstring stretches

---

### **Session 4: Upper Body (Vertical Push/Pull)**

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load | RPE | Notes |
|----------|-------------|------|-----|-------|
| Overhead Press | 3 × 5 | 60% of hypertrophy working weight | 6 | Strict form; no leg drive |
| Lat Pulldown | 3 × 6 | 60% | 6 | Full range; controlled eccentric |
| Machine Shoulder Press | 2 × 8 | 65% | 6 | Smooth, pain-free reps |
| Reverse Pec Deck | 2 × 12 | 60% | 6 | Rear delt health; light load |

**Accessory/Mobility:** 5 min band dislocations, 3 min shoulder pass-throughs

---

## Nutrition & Recovery Guidance

**Caloric Intake:**  
Maintain a slight surplus or maintenance (same as hypertrophy week). Do not drop calories aggressively—the deload is about recovery, not fat loss.

**Protein:**  
1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight daily. Consistent across all meals.

**Carbohydrates:**  
Slightly elevated on training days (5–7 g/kg) to support glycogen repletion without excess volume stress.

**Hydration:**  
3–4 liters daily; increase if sweating heavily in gym.

**Sleep:**  
Target 8–9 hours nightly. This is the primary recovery driver during deload.

**Supplementation:**  
- Creatine monohydrate: 5 g/day (continue)
- Multivitamin: daily (optional but supportive)
- Omega-3: 2–3 g EPA/DHA daily (anti-inflammatory)

---

## Additional Recovery Modalities

- **Sauna:** 10–15 min, 3–4 times during the week (if available)
- **Massage/Soft Tissue:** 30 min mid-week if accessible
- **Walking:** 20–30 min daily, low intensity
- **Stretching:** 10 min daily (static, post-session)
- **Sleep Tracking:** Monitor sleep quality; prioritize consistency

---

## Readiness Assessment (End of Week 5)

Before progressing to intensification, evaluate:

1. **Subjective Recovery:** Does the client feel mentally fresh?
2. **Sleep Quality:** Improved sleep depth/duration?
3. **Joint Health:** Any lingering aches or pains?
4. **Motivation:** Eager to train hard again?
5. **Strength Baseline:** Can he match or exceed hypertrophy-week loads at RPE 6 on compound lifts?

If all markers are positive, proceed to intensification block. If not, extend deload by 2–3 days.

---

## Notes for Your Programming

- **Exercise order** remains identical to hypertrophy block for neural consistency.
- **Rest periods** can drop to 60–90 seconds (vs. 2–3 min in hypertrophy); the low load makes this sustainable.
- **Tempo** should be deliberate and controlled—this is a skill-maintenance week, not a speed week.
- **Avoid new exercises** during deload; stick to the same movement patterns.

This week sets your client up for a strong intensification phase with reduced injury risk and restored work capacity.

---

## Strength Marker Testing (Deload Week)

**Philosophy:** Test movement quality and baseline readiness at low RPE; don't chase maxes or near-maxes.

---

## Testing Protocol

### **Session 1 (Monday) — Lower Quad**

**Test: Back Squat @ RPE 6**

| Set | Reps | Load | Purpose |
|-----|------|------|---------|
| 1 | 5 | 60% of hypertrophy working weight | Warm-up |
| 2 | 5 | 65% | Test set |
| 3 | 3 | 70% | Optional top-up (if feeling strong) |

**Record:** Weight × reps at RPE 6. Compare to Week 4 baseline.  
**Why:** Squat is low-risk; tests lower body strength recovery without fatigue.

---

### **Session 2 (Tuesday) — Upper Horizontal**

**Test: Machine Chest Press @ RPE 6**

| Set | Reps | Load | Purpose |
|-----|------|------|---------|
| 1 | 5 | 60% of hypertrophy working weight | Warm-up |
| 2 | 5 | 65% | Test set |
| 3 | 3 | 70% | Optional top-up (if feeling strong) |

**Record:** Weight × reps at RPE 6.  
**Why:** Machine press is shoulder-friendly; gives you a baseline for chest strength without aggravating his shoulder.

---

### **Session 3 (Thursday) — Lower Deadlift**

**Test: Conventional Deadlift @ RPE 6**

| Set | Reps | Load | Purpose |
|-----|------|------|---------|
| 1 | 3 | 60% of hypertrophy working weight | Warm-up |
| 2 | 3 | 65% | Test set |
| 3 | 2 | 72% | Optional top-up (if feeling strong) |

**Record:** Weight × reps at RPE 6.  
**Why:** Deadlift is the most neurally demanding; testing at low RPE tells you if CNS is recovered.

---

### **Session 4 (Friday) — Upper Vertical**

**Test: Overhead Press @ RPE 6**

| Set | Reps | Load | Purpose |
|-----|------|------|---------|
| 1 | 5 | 60% of hypertrophy working weight | Warm-up |
| 2 | 5 | 65% | Test set |
| 3 | 3 | 70% | Optional top-up (if feeling strong) |

**Record:** Weight × reps at RPE 6.  
**Why:** Vertical press tests shoulder stability and upper body strength without bench stress.

---

## Tracking Sheet Template

| Lift | Week 4 Baseline (RPE 6) | Week 5 Test (RPE 6) | Change | Notes |
|-----|-------------------------|----------------------|--------|-------|
| Back Squat | ___ × 5 | ___ × 5 | +/− ___ | Form quality? |
| Machine Chest Press | ___ × 5 | ___ × 5 | +/− ___ | Shoulder feel? |
| Conventional Deadlift | ___ × 3 | ___ × 3 | +/− ___ | Bar speed? |
| Overhead Press | ___ × 5 | ___ × 5 | +/− ___ | Stability? |

---

## Interpretation Guide

**Expected Outcomes:**

- **Strength maintained or +2–5%:** Excellent recovery; ready for intensification.
- **Strength down 5–10%:** Normal deload response; CNS is recovering; proceed as planned.
- **Strength down >10%:** Possible under-recovery; consider extending deload 2–3 days before intensification.

**Qualitative Markers to Note:**
- Bar speed (faster = better CNS recovery)
- Form quality (crisp movement = readiness)
- RPE accuracy (does RPE 6 feel genuinely light?)
- Joint comfort (especially shoulder on press movements)

---

## Key Rules for Testing

1. **No ego lifting.** These are baseline checks, not PRs.
2. **Stop if form breaks.** One rep at RPE 6 is enough; don't chase reps.
3. **Record everything.** Even small data points (weight, reps, feel) inform your intensification plan.
4. **Don't test on the same day as mobility.** Keep testing sessions clean.
5. **Rest 2–3 min between test sets.** You want accurate reads, not fatigue.

---

## Post-Testing Decision Tree

**If all four lifts are maintained or up:**  
→ Proceed to intensification block as planned. Client is ready.

**If 2–3 lifts are down 5–10%:**  
→ Proceed to intensification; monitor first week closely.

**If all four lifts are down >10%:**  
→ Extend deload by 2–3 days; retest before intensification.

This gives you objective data without compromising the deload's recovery purpose.

# **Deload Week Summary**

---

## **Weekly Schedule**

| Day | Session | Duration |
|-----|---------|----------|
| **Monday** | Session 1: Lower Quad (RPE 6) | 40 min |
| **Tuesday** | Session 2: Upper Horizontal (RPE 6) | 40 min |
| **Wednesday** | Intensity Spike: Upper Accessory (RPE 7–7.5) | 45 min |
| **Thursday** | Session 3: Lower Deadlift (RPE 6) | 45 min |
| **Friday** | Intensity Spike: Lower Accessory (RPE 7–7.5) | 45 min |
| **Saturday** | Zone 2 Cardio | 30 min |
| **Sunday** | Rest/Light Walking | Optional |

---

## **Volume Comparison**

| Metric | Hypertrophy Week (Weeks 1–4) | Deload Week | Change |
|--------|------------------------------|-------------|--------|
| **Working Sets per Session** | 18 | 7–8 | **−58%** |
| **Weekly Total** | 72 sets | 42 sets | **−42%** |
| **Sessions per Week** | 4 | 5 (3 deload + 2 intensity spikes) | +1 session |

**Breakdown:**
- 3 baseline deload sessions (Mon, Tue, Thu): 22 working sets @ RPE 6
- 2 intensity spike sessions (Wed, Fri): 20 working sets @ RPE 7–7.5

---

## **Intensity Comparison**

| Metric | Hypertrophy Week | Deload Week |
|--------|------------------|-------------|
| **RPE (Baseline Sessions)** | 8.5 | 6 |
| **RPE (Intensity Spikes)** | — | 7–7.5 |
| **Load (Baseline)** | 100% (working weight) | 60–65% |
| **Load (Intensity Spikes)** | — | 75% |
| **Reps in Reserve** | 1–2 | 3–4 (baseline); 2–3 (spikes) |

---

## **Exercise Selection**

**Maintained from Hypertrophy Block:**
- Back Squat, Leg Press, Leg Extension (Lower Quad)
- Machine Chest Press (swapped from Bench), Barbell Rows, Face Pulls (Upper Horizontal)
- Conventional Deadlift, Romanian Deadlift, Leg Curl, Sled Push (Lower Deadlift)
- Overhead Press, Lat Pulldown, Reverse Pec Deck (Upper Vertical)

**Added for Intensity Spikes:**
- Incline Dumbbell Press, Weighted Dips, Machine Shoulder Press (Wed)
- Front Squat, Trap Bar Deadlift, Bulgarian Split Squat (Fri)

---

## **Additional Components**

| Component | Duration | Frequency |
|-----------|----------|-----------|
| Mobility | 20 min | Integrated into sessions |
| Zone 2 Cardio | 30 min | 1 session (Saturday) |
| Strength Testing | Embedded | 4 lifts (one per strength session) |

---

## **Key Outcomes**

✓ **58% volume reduction** from hypertrophy block  
✓ **RPE 6 baseline** allows genuine recovery  
✓ **RPE 7–7.5 spikes** maintain engagement and work capacity  
✓ **Shoulder-friendly** (machine press, incline DB, dips)  
✓ **Movement patterns preserved** for motor learning continuity  
✓ **Strength testing embedded** to track readiness for intensification  

**Total weekly training time:** ~4.75 hours (vs. ~5.5 hours in hypertrophy week)

---

Ready to move into intensification block pending strength test results.
